comparator.sourceNotes: Annual BA-KOR programme groups and module records establish the 180 EC Leiden-based Korean 3 example. The year-two Themes and Approaches group and module both carry 10 EC. Year three has 15 EC of specialist choices, a 5 EC thesis seminar, a 10 EC final paper and 30 EC of genuinely open study. Mentorship carries zero credit. Korean 1 requires prior Hangeul literacy, Korean 2 follows Korean 1 and Korean 3 follows Korean 2. Korean language in use and both selected intermediate reading courses follow Korean 3. Topical Reading requires completion of years one and two. Business Korean follows all year-two language courses. The topical seminar is completed in semester one before the thesis seminar. The final paper requires completion of years one and two and first-semester year-three courses, plus enrollment in or completion of the thesis seminar.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Current workbook evidence credits experimental language research, close reading, audiovisual and documentary methods, comparative empire including Chinese examples, qualitative inquiry, comparative politics, geopolitics and macroeconomic modelling. Researching the American Century develops source analysis and a substantial paper on its current historical focus. The advanced regional and Korean-language work required to anchor a Korean studies response is not taught across the available composition. The course-comparability evidence records the tested proposals.

candidateAssessment.concept: Korean language, literature and cultural media
candidateAssessment.assessment: UCR supplies literary, film, media, rhetoric and heritage methods, but no Korean-language instruction and no documented Korean literature, media, cultural tradition or material-heritage sequence. Filling 23 non-PPD places with generic methods would remove the Korean object that defines the direction.

candidateAssessment.concept: Korean history, society and the divided peninsula
candidateAssessment.assessment: Modern history, empire, sociology and qualitative methods are genuine analytic foundations, but the documented course content does not provide Korean history, the division of the peninsula, North Korean communism, South Korean capitalism or sustained social-science study of Korea.

candidateAssessment.concept: Korea in regional politics and economic development
candidateAssessment.assessment: Comparative politics, international relations and international macroeconomics supply transferable frameworks. They do not offer a Korea- or East Asia-centred politics and development sequence, so expanding them to a full programme would become generic international studies rather than a defensible response to the stated Korean Studies interest.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Korean Studies bachelor combines Korean language and source work with the history, society, culture and politics of Korea. It places North and South Korea in a regional and global context and concludes with supervised research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related methods in language research, literary and media analysis, comparative history, politics and economics. A full programme built from those courses would focus mainly on general methods and on regions other than Korea. Leiden sustains the study of Korean language, history and society through advanced work with Korean-language sources. The related UCR courses provide useful starting points, but do not form a sufficiently close alternative for this degree.

curriculum.limitation: The example totals 180 EC and selects Korean 3 at Leiden in year two. Year three includes 30 EC of open electives, 15 EC of specialist choices, a 5 EC thesis seminar and a 10 EC final paper. The final paper requires completion of years one and two and the first semester of year three, plus enrolment in or completion of the thesis seminar.

componentNotes.curr-5721vko8y: Students should be able to read and write Hangeul before starting Korean 1.

componentNotes.curr-5723vkbky: This option requires completion of the second-year Korean language courses.
componentNotes.curr-5723kt09y: A first-semester content seminar on modern Korean society and politics, using English scholarship and Korean-language material.

componentNotes.curr-5723vscry: A supervised research paper of about 10,000 words, normally written in Dutch or English. Assessment includes substantive use of Korean-language material.
